examples.text: Seine Augen schauen nervös umher, er gestikuliert wild, wirkt unruhig. (...) Der 56-Jährige, der sonst wie ein unbeweglicher Stein dasitzt, klingt flehentlich, während er spricht.
examples.translation: Ses yeux regardent nerveusement autour de lui, il gesticule frénétiquement, semble agité. (...) L’homme de 56 ans, habituellement assis comme une pierre immobile, a un ton suppliant lorsqu’il parle.

examples.text: „Das war ein feiner Junge, bloß stotterte er mächtig, es dauerte lange, bis er was raushatte, darum machte er auch so große flehentliche Augen.“

glosses: present participle and gerund of implore
The act of one who implores; imploration.

examples.text: But on the night that Nekhludov seduces Maslova, he forces his way past doors, implorings, and physical resistance.

glosses: The act of making a plea.

examples.text: But it pleased her to play on my passion / And whet me to pleadings / That won from her mirthful negations / And scornings undue.

glosses: A document filed in a lawsuit, particularly a document initiating litigation or responding to the initiation of litigation.
present participle and gerund of plead

examples.text: Franchise, relaxed and soothed by the vagueness of a surrender set so far in the future, simply took hold of his two hands to make him behave himself and looked at him with her pretty pleading eyes — the eyes of a sensitive woman who didn't want to risk having a child by anyone but her husband.
With a pleading look, she raised her eyes to him.
Have but a pleading heart and God will have a plenteous hand.

Private-equity nabobs bristle at being dubbed mere financiers. Piling debt onto companies’ balance-sheets is only a small part of what leveraged buy-outs are about, they insist. Improving the workings of the businesses they take over is just as core to their calling, if not more so. Much of their pleading is public-relations bluster.
